title: `project_file_unwritable` can claim nothing changed after an earlier write landed
description: Found while fixing WCLI-7 (the review's F4 class, one step further out). src/contract/errors.ts declares project_file_unwritable as 'Ward could not read or write a project file. Nothing was changed.' A single-target run makes that true, but ward init writes the manifest and then each selected bridge file, and the write of a later target can fail (unwritable or read-only file, a write error) after an earlier one has landed via temp-file-and-rename. The error then reports that nothing was changed while a file in the repository has, in fact, changed. Not fixed in WCLI-7 because it changes a user-facing contract string outside that task's review fix list; recorded here rather than left silent. Related and deliberately NOT in scope: whether the fix is a truthful rewording or a reordering is a design decision, and the same question applies to any multi-file command that reports a single 'nothing changed' claim.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The message a failed multi-file write reports is true in every path that raises it: a test makes the second of two targets unwritable after the first has been written, and asserts the reported text does not claim that nothing was changed (and documents what it does claim)

No other error in the catalog carries an unqualified nothing-was-changed claim in a path that can follow a successful write; each is either verified single-target or reworded, and the audit is recorded in the task notes

plan: 2. Contract: reword project_file_unwritable to "Ward could not read or write a project file. Ward did not change it." and vault_busy to "Another Ward process held the vault for too long. The vault was not changed." (DEC-10 Option A, accepted; the first sentence is unchanged, only the unqualified reassurance is scoped).

3. Test (AC1): in project-binding.test.ts, make the checkout root read-only with .ward writable so the manifest lands and the CLAUDE.md write fails; assert exit 4, code project_file_unwritable, the manifest changed on disk, and the reported text scoped to a project file rather than claiming nothing changed.
4. Audit (AC2): record the per-entry verdicts for the five catalog entries carrying the claim, with the raise sites and write ordering that make each true.
5. Records and gates: task notes for the DEC-10 reading and the audit; bun run check; lore check --strict; independent review over the diff; PR into dev with CI green; merge bare, then promote.
implementationNotes:
WCLI-27 IMPLEMENTED (2026-09-29, branch feat/WCLI-27-honest-nothing-changed). DESIGN SOURCE READ FIRST-PARTY, not relayed: DEC-10 at opum-ai/opum-agent origin/main, .quest/planning.json decisions[9], status accepted, outcome "ACCEPTED: OPTION A, REWORD, as the packet scopes it. ... The approved strings: project_file_unwritable becomes 'Ward could not read or write a project file. Ward did not change it.' and vault_busy becomes 'The vault was not changed.' NOT AUTHORISED: the variant 'A plus a separate no-partial-write task'." That variant is not filed, and no reorder or no-partial-write work is in this change.

A READING OF DEC-10, STATED BECAUSE THE RECORD ADMITS TWO. The outcome quotes vault_busy's replacement as the reassurance alone ("The vault was not changed.") where it quotes project_file_unwritable's as a whole message. I took the narrower change: the diagnostic sentence "Another Ward process held the vault for too long." is kept and only the unqualified reassurance is replaced. Reasons, in order: (1) minimal change -- the other reading DELETES existing text, which would itself be a change beyond the two approved strings, and DEC-10's own scope clause binds this approval to the option text as written; (2) DEC-10 names the catalog's existing house style as the model, and every sibling entry is a diagnostic plus a scoped claim (vault_store_unrecognized, project_path_unsafe, project_manifest_malformed); (3) vault_busy's own hint, "Retry once the other Ward command has finished", names a cause that only the kept sentence states. If the intent was the wholesale replacement, the difference is one sentence on one line.

WHAT SHIPPED. src/contract/errors.ts: project_file_unwritable now reads "Ward could not read or write a project file. Ward did not change it." and vault_busy now reads "Another Ward process held the vault for too long. The vault was not changed." Each carries a comment naming the write path that made the old claim false. No error type, code, hint or envelope shape changed, so exit codes are untouched.

AC1 MEASURED TWICE, AND THE PAIR IS THE EVIDENCE. test/project-binding.test.ts gains a describe, "WCLI-27: a failed write reports a claim scoped to the file it failed on", holding one test. The scenario is the one WCLI-27 names: the checkout root is chmod 0555 with .ward writable, so the manifest lands and the CLAUDE.md write that follows it fails. FIXED TREE: 32 pass, 0 fail on the file; bun run check exits 0 with 426 pass, 0 fail, 2164 expect() calls across 18 files. PRE-FIX TREE, same invocation, errors.ts stashed: 31 pass, 1 fail, and the only failure is this test's message assertion -- "Expected to contain: 'Ward did not change it.' / Received: 'Ward could not read or write a project file. Nothing was changed.'". The premise assertions (the manifest exists on disk, CLAUDE.md does not) passed on BOTH trees, which is what localises the red to the string rather than to the scenario or the harness: the pre-fix code really does let the manifest land and then report that nothing was changed. The test asserts the premise as well as the text for the same reason -- a message-only assertion would still pass if the write order changed later and the string became true for a different reason.

GATES. bun run check exit 0 (typecheck, lint, format:check, layer:check 36 files 0 violations, 426 tests). lore check --strict exit 0, 11 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Both measured on this branch before the PR opened. CI results are on the PR, not claimed here.

AC2 AUDIT, per catalog entry carrying an unqualified nothing-was-changed claim. Five entries carried the exact string "Nothing was changed" at this branch's base, 99880fa (grep src/contract/errors.ts). Two are false in the sense WCLI-27 names and are the two DEC-10 rewords; three are clean and are deliberately left alone. Each verdict is given with the raise sites and the write ordering that decide it, so a later reader can re-derive it rather than trust it.

FALSE, REWORDED. (1) project_file_unwritable -- raise sites src/adapters/project-files.ts:57, :178, :214, :243. The one that can follow a landed write is :214 in atomicWrite, reached from src/application/project.ts:230-233, which writes the manifest and then each selected bridge file in target order, so a later target failing leaves the manifest already renamed into place. (2) vault_busy -- raise site src/adapters/sqlite-vault-store.ts:253. Two paths reach it after a write: src/application/project.ts:307-311 prepares, and therefore writes, the project files before :320 registerForProject's store.mutate can raise it; and src/application/backup.ts:179 stores the key before :180 store.create can raise it. The vault transaction itself rolls back, which is why the reword narrows the claim to the vault instead of dropping it.

CLEAN, VERIFIED SINGLE-TARGET, NOT REWORDED. (3) setup_in_progress -- raise sites src/adapters/setup-session.ts:114, :141, :152, :237, all inside lock acquisition. src/cli/main.ts:101 makes acquireSetupSession the first statement of setupCommand, before the store or the key provider is constructed. The only write that can precede it is setup-session.ts:189 prepareVaultDirectory, which creates the directory only when it is absent -- and every raise site requires a lock file INSIDE that same directory to exist, so in every path that raises, the directory already existed before this run touched anything. (4) backup_malformed -- reachable only through parseBackup (src/domain/backup.ts:311, with decodeBase64 at :301 and :307 and ownRecord beneath it) and openBackup (:252), and those are called only at src/application/backup.ts:167 and :169, both before the first write at :179. runBackup parses no backup: it calls sealBackup and encodeBackup and writes last, at src/application/backup.ts:116-117. (5) backup_open_failed -- one raise site, src/domain/backup.ts:266 inside openBackup, reached only from src/application/backup.ts:169, again before the first write at :179.

COVERAGE, stated because it is the part that does not travel with the verdicts. This audit is over the string "Nothing was changed", which is the claim WCLI-27 names. It is NOT an audit of every claim that a change did not happen: vault_store_unrecognized, project_manifest_malformed, project_path_unsafe, instructions_markers_conflict and others say "Ward did not change it" and were not re-checked here. They were out of this task's scope by its own wording, and none of them is known to be false -- but none of them is verified here either, and the next reader should not read this note as clearing them.

NO BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Before the change, no test, doc, fixture or script pinned any of the five strings: grep over src, test, docs and scripts for the claim and for both rewordings returns nothing outside src/contract/errors.ts, which is why the two edits broke no test. The only file that quotes the old text afterwards is WCLI-27's own description, which is a record of the finding and is left as written rather than rewritten to match the fix.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW OVER PR opum-ai/ward-cli#51 (2026-09-29, opum-workflow:reviewer, one specialist dispatched alone, over origin/dev 99880fa..94686f1). The reviewer worked from a Lore context pack (profile review, non-degraded, 12 sections, packDigest sha256:a8735533e164309061410f865b65acfa8237410e8a32f20d1078e18136578e48) and found, as the dispatch expected, that the pack carries the ADRs but no Ward source and neither DEC-10 nor this task -- so it read those first-party too. Its tree discipline was verified: it could not use git stash (the change is committed, so there was nothing to stash) and used git restore --source=origin/dev --worktree instead, restoring to the branch tip and confirming empty status and byte-identical shas afterwards.

WHAT IT CONFIRMED, INDEPENDENTLY AND BY MEASUREMENT. AC1 is met and the new test is real: 32 pass / 0 fail on the branch; with base errors.ts in the worktree, 31 pass / 1 fail with the failure at the message assertion only, so the premise assertions at test/project-binding.test.ts:855-856 passed on the pre-fix tree and the red is localised to the string. It also measured the failure mode the test's finally block prevents rather than assuming it: in bun 1.3.14 rmSync of the shared root fails EACCES/ENOTEMPTY when a 0555 directory with entries remains, so without the restore the file's own afterAll would leave the tmp tree behind. And it answered the question I put to it by mutation rather than judgement -- flipping prepare's two writes in src/application/project.ts (restored byte-identical afterwards) reddens the manifest premise assertion at :855 and nothing else in the file, which shows the premise assertion is the ONLY guard on that write order and that a message-only assertion would have accepted the string in the reordered path. Corollary worth carrying: a future sanctioned option-B/transactional implementation will redden this test even though the message stays true, and it will need revising deliberately rather than read as a regression.

F1, HIGH, AND THE REASON THIS IS NOT MERGED YET. The reviewer reads DEC-10's outcome as requiring the WHOLE vault_busy message, not just its reassurance: both clauses use "becomes", the first quotes a whole message whose own first sentence happens to be unchanged, so the record's convention is that the quoted string is the post-state message. On that reading the shipped "Another Ward process held the vault for too long. The vault was not changed." is not one of the two approved strings, and the first sentence is text the approval did not authorise keeping. My contrary reading (and the three reasons for it) is in the note above and in the PR body. I could not settle it first-party: I searched opum-agent's tree at origin/main and opum-doc's at origin/main for the original packet text and for either string, and the packet survives only as DEC-10's rendering -- DEC-10 never quotes vault_busy's CURRENT text, so the question is a reading of a relay, and neither reading can be refuted from the record. The reviewer also observed that the retained sentence is an unhedged causal claim while sqlite-vault-store.ts:253 maps any SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED to vault_busy and a non-contention failure is reported the same way, so keeping it buys back an exposure the one-sentence version does not have. ROUTED to opum-agent as the design authority rather than decided here; the PR is complete and green behind it. This is a one-line difference whichever way it goes.

F2, LOW, AND IT CORRECTS THIS TASK'S OWN AC2 NOTE. The setup_in_progress justification in the audit note is false as written; see the correction note that follows this one. A third string is outside DEC-10's approval, so nothing is reworded here -- the corrected verdict is recorded and the rewording question is routed alongside F1.

F3, LOW. The backup_malformed reachability claim in the audit note is inaccurate; the verdict survives and the corrected statement is in the note that follows.

F4, LOW, FLAGGED AND ROUTED, NOT FIXED. docs/adr/0001-vault-storage-and-key-custody.md:178-179 still records "Past the busy timeout they report vault_busy, and nothing is changed" -- the broad formulation DEC-10 measured false in two paths, left standing in the design record after this change narrows only the catalog. Read at vault-store level it agrees with the new string; read at run level it is the sentence the change exists to stop asserting. It is a lore edit, not this PR's, and rewording a design record is not mine to do: routed with a proposed minimal edit that reuses the already-approved phrase ("and the vault is not changed.") so it needs no new wording from anyone.

F5, BELOW THE REPORTING BAR, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE ONE PLACE THE NEW STRING IS NOT LITERALLY EXHAUSTIVE. healJournalMode (src/adapters/sqlite-vault-store.ts:298-304) runs PRAGMA journal_mode = DELETE before the immediate transaction, so a persist/truncate vault's header can be rewritten by Ward and a later vault_busy then say "The vault was not changed." Contents are unchanged, the mode is healed to Ward's own canonical state, and the window is microseconds. Not acted on; recorded so the next reader of that sentence has it.

AC2 VERDICT UNDER REVIEW: met with a caveat, and the caveat is recorded rather than smoothed. The audit's scope is the literal string "Nothing was changed", which is narrower than AC2's phrase "an unqualified nothing-was-changed claim". The note declares the excluded entries and says plainly that none of them is verified there, and the reviewer judges that the difference between a declared partial audit and the fleet's certified-weaker-clause failure -- but it is a caveat, not a clean pass. One entry the reviewer checked and cleared that the audit does not name: project_manifest_malformed can be raised at src/application/project.ts:348 after Ward's own successful write to that same file, but its claim is scoped to the offending document, which is DEC-10's own approved house style.

AC2 AUDIT, CORRECTIONS (2026-09-29, forced by the independent review of PR opum-ai/ward-cli#51 and verified first-hand before being written here). This note supersedes two statements in the AC2 audit note above. Both were errors of JUSTIFICATION rather than of arithmetic, and both were found by a reviewer that re-derived the raise sites instead of reading the note -- which is exactly what that note invited a later reader to do, so the defect was in the note's reasoning and not in the instruction to distrust it.

CORRECTION 1: setup_in_progress -- the stated reason was FALSE, and the verdict narrows to a judgement. The audit note argued: "every raise site requires a lock file INSIDE that same directory to exist, so in every path that raises, the directory already existed before this run touched anything." That is wrong. src/adapters/setup-session.ts:99-103 opens the lock path with O_CREAT, so the raise at :114 does not require a lock file to pre-exist; the site's own comment at :110-111 says a NON-contention flock failure is reported as setup_in_progress too; and off macOS the second-attempt raise at :237 follows clearStaleLock, which may rmSync a stale setup.lock at :154 -- this run deleting a stale lock and then reporting that nothing was changed. So two paths can change something before the raise: (a) on macOS, :189 prepareVaultDirectory may create an absent vault directory and a non-contention flock failure then reports it (a create-and-flock race with a concurrent setup reaches the same place); (b) off macOS, the stale-lock deletion above. The verdict that survives is narrower and IS a judgement, not a construction: the contention path cannot follow a change, because another process holds a lock inside a directory that must already exist; and on the shipped platform the only preceding change is an empty private vault directory that the documented retry creates anyway. NOT REWORDED HERE -- a third string is outside DEC-10's approval, which binds this change to two. Routed to opum-agent as a candidate for a third reword, for the design authority to decide rather than this session.

CORRECTION 2: backup_malformed -- the reachability claim was wrong, the verdict is unaffected. The audit note said backup_malformed is "reachable only through parseBackup ... and openBackup ... and those are called only at src/application/backup.ts:167 and :169". That is not the whole set. The code also raises it from ownBytes (src/domain/backup.ts:95, raising at :96 and :100), ownKdf (:107, raising at :109), ownHeader (:131, raising at :133, :137 and :143), ownRecord (:152, raising at :162), sealBackup (:210, raising at :217) and encodeBackup (:276 through ownRecord) -- and those run in runBackup at src/application/backup.ts:111, :112 and :116, and in runRestore at :168. The verdict is UNCHANGED, and the reason to record is one that does not depend on any caller list: every raise site precedes the first write of the command that reaches it, because runBackup's only write is :117 and runRestore's are :179-180, and nothing parses a backup after :180. That is the correct statement of why this entry is clean; the narrower reachability claim was not.

UNCHANGED BY THIS NOTE: the project_file_unwritable verdict (raise sites src/adapters/project-files.ts:57, :178, :214, :243, with the landed-write path at :214 reached from src/application/project.ts:230-233); the vault_busy verdict (single raise site src/adapters/sqlite-vault-store.ts:253, with the two post-write paths at src/application/project.ts:307-320 and src/application/backup.ts:179-180, and the vault transaction genuinely rolling back because mutations run inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE); and backup_open_failed (one raise site, src/domain/backup.ts:266 inside openBackup, reached only from src/application/backup.ts:169, before the write at :179). The reviewer re-derived each of these and they hold as written.
